entries.text: My dear students! How ARE you all today?\nFeeling good, I hope?[VAR 0x0114(002C)]
entries.label: class_d_01_language_01

entries.text: Je m’appelle Salvatore. My name is Salvatore![VAR 0x0114(0026)]
entries.label: class_d_01_language_02

entries.text: Merci beaucoup! That is, thank you very much for\nyour attention here in my class![VAR 0x0114(0026)]
entries.label: class_d_01_language_03

entries.text: I’m so heureux—or happy—for this chance to\nre-experience my younger days with you all![VAR 0x0114(0026)]
entries.label: class_d_01_language_04

entries.text: Do you know what “Salvatore” means? It means\n“savior”! So just imagine I’m here to SAVE you\r\nfrom spooooky new languages. Haha! Funny, no?[VAR 0x0114(0026)]
entries.label: class_d_01_language_05

entries.text: That’s right! My classes will teach you about\nvarious languages from different regions.[VAR 0x0114(0026)]
entries.label: class_d_01_language_06

entries.text: You may say “Good morning!” or “Hello!” as a\ngreeting, but people from elsewhere may say\r\n“Bonjour!” or “Salut!”[VAR 0x0114(0026)]
entries.label: class_d_01_language_07

entries.text: I’ve heard there’s even a popular streamer out\nthere who smashes several languages together\r\nand says “’Ello, ’ello, hola! Ciao and bonjour!”[VAR 0x0114(0026)]
entries.label: class_d_01_language_08

entries.text: There are so many regions out there in our world,\nand each can have their own unique languages![VAR 0x0114(0026)]
entries.label: class_d_01_language_09

entries.text: Gracias, merci, xièxie, arigato, danke—these all\nhave the same meaning! Can you guess what it is?[VAR 0x0114(0026)]
entries.label: class_d_01_language_10

entries.text: Good-bye
entries.label: class_d_01_select_01

entries.text: Thank you
entries.label: class_d_01_select_02

entries.text: Good night
entries.label: class_d_01_select_03

entries.text: Oh! [VAR 0x0100(0000)], was it?\c\nThat’s not quite right, but your willingness to\nspeak up will serve you well in language learning![VAR 0x0114(0026)]
entries.label: class_d_01_language_answer_01

entries.text: Waouh! [VAR 0x0100(0000)], was it?\c\nBrav[VAR 0x1100(00FF,0101)]oa! That’s correct! And speaking up is\nimportant in language learning, too![VAR 0x0114(0026)]
entries.label: class_d_01_language_answer_02

entries.text: Oh! [VAR 0x0100(0000)], was it?\c\nThat’s not quite right, but your willingness to\nspeak up will serve you well in language learning![VAR 0x0114(0026)]
entries.label: class_d_01_language_answer_03

entries.text: Gracias, merci, xièxie—these words all mean\n“thank you.” I guess some of you probably knew\r\nat least one of those![VAR 0x0114(0026)]
entries.label: class_d_01_language_11

entries.text: Despite meaning the same thing, their lengths\nand sounds are all different! Isn’t that interesting?[VAR 0x0114(0026)]
entries.label: class_d_01_language_12

entries.text: And now, apropos of nothing, let me give you\nall one of my wise words of advice![VAR 0x0114(0026)]
entries.label: class_d_01_language_13

entries.text: When you travel abroad, you should try to speak\nthe local language as much as you can—even if\r\nyou can’t speak it very well![VAR 0x0114(0026)]
entries.label: class_d_01_language_14

entries.text: I’m sure your willingness to try will make the\npeople you meet très heureux—very happy![VAR 0x0114(0026)]
entries.label: class_d_01_language_15

entries.text: Honestly, from my experience, just being able to\nsay “hello,” “delicious,” and “thank you” in the\r\nlocal language will get you pretty far.[VAR 0x0114(0026)]
entries.label: class_d_01_language_16

entries.text: For everything else, just pretend you’re Mr. Mime\nand gesture away![VAR 0x0114(0026)]
entries.label: class_d_01_language_17

entries.text: Oh! There’s that pesky bell. I guess that’s all the\ntime we have for today![VAR 0x0114(0026)]
entries.label: class_d_01_language_18

entries.text: Well, adios! Mata ne! À la prochaine! See you\nlater, everyone![VAR 0x0114(0026)]
entries.label: class_d_01_language_19
